newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE president urges Iran to respond on islands.
newsitem.headline: UAE president urges Iran to respond on islands.

text.p: United Arab Emirates (UAE) President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan on Monday called on Iran to respond to an appeal for a peaceful solution to their dispute over three islands in the Gulf.

Sheikh Zaid, in a speech marking the UAE's 25th anniversary, said the country would continue to work to regain the islands of Greater and Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa located near key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.

"We now renew, therefore, our call to the Islamic Republic of Iran to respond positively to our initiatives and appeals to reach a peaceful solution to the dispute over the three islands, either through serious bilateral negotiations, or through an acceptance of the referral of the issue to the International Court of Justice," he said.
The 78-year-old UAE leader, whose speech was read for him in the capital Abu Dhabi by an assistant, added:

"From our side, we have shown our goodwill towards Iran in more than one fashion, and on more than one occasion, sufficiently so for them to decide upon their own options, based upon our historic links, our friendly relations, good neighbourliness and the mutual interests that exist between us."
The UAE had the support of the Gulf Cooperation Council, the Arab League and other friendly countries, he said.
Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable and described an Arab summit stand earlier this year backing the UAE's claim as likely to increase tension in the region.
It has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any misunderstandings.

Iran's new ambassador in Abu Dhabi said a month ago Tehran was about to launch a new round of talks with the UAE to resolve the dispute. Ambassador Hussein Sadiqi was previously Iran's chief negotiator with the UAE over the islands.

The UAE and Iran have been at loggerheads over the islands since 1992 when the UAE accused Iran of occupying them and revived its territorial claim after Iran tightened security measures at Abu Musa. Iran and UAE member Sharjah ran Abu Musa jointly under a 1971 agreement.
